purpose: Decide which mechanism to discharge next, on measured counts rather than on the size of a file list. Aggregated from the applied v1u closure; no site bodies were re-audited here, so every figure is a work-planning figure, not a safety result.
uniform_blocking_cause: mechanism state is OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED and the owning boundary does not cover the site (covers_site=false); contract_basis is 'block-level SAFETY present but no # Safety fn contract'. Every blocked site is UNSAFE_FN_DEF.

clusters.abstraction: SLH-DSA Adrs + hash state over exclusive &mut
X.509 v3 extension codecs; per-extension semantics, >=8 signature families
one ConfCmdFn signature and one SslConfCmdTbl.cmd slot
SSL_CONF option-list / min-max helpers over SslConfCtx

recommendation.why: Smallest self-contained mechanism (41 files, all under src/ssl); 13 of 18 blocked sites fall in two genuine callback abstractions (S1 and S2/S3); S1 needs one reusable proof (valid exclusive SslConfCtx for the callback duration, valid NUL-terminated value, no retention after return); highest security consequence among the tractable mechanisms (protocol version, cipher suite, verification mode, session policy).
recommendation.scope_caveat: The narrow defensible scope is the 18 reachable sites / 5 files; the broad scope is the 41-file state.json mechanism set. The claim must name one; the effort rises roughly 8x if the broad scope is chosen. AGENTS.md section 22 forbids silently substituting a narrower scope.

rejections.why: section 7 clause 3 cannot be established without measured concurrency evidence; no Loom/TSan evidence exists. A static contract would be documentation-only.
a mechanism-wide record would assert coverage of 40 src/runtime/bio files while 73 SSL BIO sites remain unaudited; false coverage is forbidden by section 7.
371 files / 90,830 unsafe ops / 5 of 32 families measured, and at least four distinct ownership interiors; mechanism-wide cost dwarfs the 101-site benefit.
75 sites across 31 per-extension codecs with distinct types and i2r/v2i/i2v/s2i/i2s/print/audit semantics; a shared template comment would not satisfy a per-operation validity contract.
the residual 13 split across CMS ASN.1 callbacks, DRBG construction, a CMS freefunc and a PKCS7 callback in three subsystems; one record would conflate four interiors.
cross-cutting ABI class with no file-count scope; mechanism-wide discharge would be a crate-wide unsafe extern "C" claim. Its 17 existing records are correctly scoped boundaries.

evidence_required_for_recommendation: frozen identity S plus a separate evidence commit E; rebuild once and bind the downstream executable digest
fn-level # Safety on all 18 blocked unsafe fns and on every other unsafe op in the declared scope; per-site receipt for S1-S4; hidden = 0
caller/edge closure: every write of SslConfCmdTbl.cmd, every dispatch site, SslConfCtx provenance and exclusivity, reentrancy analysis, per-call-site witnesses
three independent axes: ABI/functional differential, Rust soundness (Miri Stacked and Tree Borrows), crypto/security policy decisions
independent adjudication by a reviewer who is not the author
negative_controls: aliasing canary across the callback; Miri Stacked and Tree Borrows must fire, or an ASan harness with a poisoned sentinel
use-after-free/reentrancy canary: handler stashes the ctx, a second command after SSL_CONF_CTX_free; ASan must fire
wrong-release canary at the owner seam; allocator-seam canary must fire
confirm each canary actually fires on an intentionally vulnerable build; a silent instrument fails the claim
non_claims: These are work-planning counts from the applied v1u closure, not safety results.
No mechanism is discharged by this map; SAFE_COMPATIBLE remains 0/33.
File counts come from state.json's mechanism file sets; reachability differs from file membership and the distinction is load-bearing for section 7 scope.
